title: Example App Staging
heading: Example App: what is deployed in staging
lede: A fictional web app on a managed Kubernetes cluster. Users sign in with an OIDC identity provider and reach the app over public HTTPS; operators reach the admin tools over a private tailnet; Argo CD deploys everything from git. Pick a flow to follow it step by step. Hover or tap any box for details.
meta: Built from infra/terraform/envs/staging, deploy/argocd/staging and docs/operations on main. Desired state, not a live query. No IP addresses, IDs or secrets are shown.
callout: Read this first. App users do not use the tailnet. They reach the app over public HTTPS with their identity-provider token (flow 1). The tailnet is the private door for operators to Argo CD and Grafana (flow 2).
footer: Generated with the architecture-diagram skill from the repository's desired state.

flows.name: 1 · App user
flows.why: How a user signs in and uses the app.
steps: The browser or desktop app sends the user to the identity provider (OIDC with PKCE) and gets an access token.
The app calls app.<domain> over HTTPS; the cloud load balancer passes the traffic to the cluster.
ingress-nginx terminates TLS and routes the request to the web app.
The web app calls the API, which verifies the token on every request and reads PostgreSQL.
Slow work goes to a Redis queue that the background worker consumes.

flows.name: 2 · Operator via tailnet
flows.why: How the team reaches the admin tools, which have no public route.
steps: The operator's laptop is on the tailnet; a WireGuard tunnel reaches the in-cluster Tailscale node.
The node forwards :8080 to Argo CD and :3000 to Grafana. Each tool keeps its own login.
kubectl does not use the tailnet: it goes to the Kubernetes API with cloud IAM.

flows.name: 3 · Deploy (CI + GitOps)
flows.why: How a merged pull request becomes running pods, with no stored cloud keys.
steps: A pull request merges into main; GitHub Actions validates it and builds images.
Actions pushes the images to the registry with OIDC federation (keyless).
Argo CD reads main with a read-only deploy key.
Argo CD applies every Application in sync waves, with prune and self-heal.
Nodes pull the images from the registry.

flows.name: 4 · Secrets & certificates
flows.why: Why no secret lives in git.
steps: External Secrets reads the cloud secret manager through workload identity.
It writes the Kubernetes Secrets the app needs (database URL, OIDC client, API keys).
cert-manager gets public TLS certificates from Let's Encrypt.

flows.name: 5 · Observability
flows.why: Where to look when something breaks.
steps: Alloy ships container logs to Loki.
Grafana reads metrics from Prometheus and logs from Loki.
Prometheus fires alerts; the notification receiver is still planned.

flows.name: 6 · Data & backups
flows.why: Where data lives and how it is backed up.
steps: User uploads and PostgreSQL backups (CloudNativePG + Barman) go to object storage over the S3 API.
PostgreSQL itself runs in the cluster, managed by the CloudNativePG operator.
